item.title: Exact Spelling For Repair Logo

turns.text: I need a square logo for my repair shop. The name is KwickFixx — please spell it exactly like that, with capital K and F and two x's. Small orange wrench, black lettering, white background. No slogan.

item.tests: Preserves an intentionally unusual business spelling and capitalization in the rendered logo.

answer_sheet.Exact name and capitalization: KwickFixx, with uppercase K and F and two lowercase x characters at the end.
answer_sheet.Visual style and colors: A simple repair-shop logo with a small orange wrench and black lettering on white.

must_haves: The rendered name reads exactly 'KwickFixx', preserving spelling and capitalization.
The name is legible and not obscured by the mark.
A small orange wrench accompanies black lettering.
The background is white and there is no slogan or additional text.

turns.text: i need a logo for my repair shop

dialog.agent:
Happy to make you a logo. One quick question first:

**Where will this be shown or posted (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, a website, print, somewhere else)?**

It would also help to know:
- **The shop's name** or any other words you want on the logo, spelled exactly how you want them. Or tell me if you'd like it with no text.
- **What you repair** (cars, phones, bikes, appliances…) and any style or colors you like, such as bold and modern, vintage, or minimal.
dialog.why: The assistant asks where the logo will be used, the shop name, and what the shop repairs, then waits for the answers before making anything.
dialog.user: idk, i just need it square

turns.agent:
I couldn't make your logo. Magic Hour refused the request because your account doesn't have enough credits. Nothing was created.

I'd already chosen the cheapest option for your free plan: one square image at 640px, which costs about 5 credits. So a different setting won't fix this. You'll need more credits first, either by waiting for your free credits to refill or by adding credits on your Magic Hour account.

Once you have credits, tell me and I'll make it. I've planned a square logo of a crossed wrench and screwdriver in a round badge, in a simple flat style on a white background, with no text. If you want your shop's name on it, send it spelled exactly how you want it. You can also tell me what you repair or which colors you like, so the logo fits your shop better.
